title: Tight Conglomerate Core
story: A tight cluster of banks that prop each other up. Six core banks guarantee each other's debt so tightly that the system has two stable moods: everything stands, or the whole core falls together. A short simulation that only explores one mood will confidently tell you the wrong bank to bail out.
verdict: QeMCMC ranked the targets correctly at 4,000 steps; classical MH needed 12,000 -- a 3x iteration-budget gap. Both converge eventually, but under a fixed budget the wrong ranking means the wrong bailout.

title: Rush-Hour Gridlock
story: A city grid at rush hour, one closure from gridlock. Closing the wrong street at the wrong hour doesn't just slow one block -- traffic reroutes and jams somewhere else. The worst street is only visible once you've seen both the free-flowing and the gridlocked regime.
verdict: QeMCMC ranked the widening targets correctly at 8,000 steps; classical MH needed the full 20,000 -- a 2.5x iteration-budget gap, and the only arm whose final ranking matches the exact answer exactly (rho = 1.0).

title: Fragile Periphery, Hidden Amplifier
story: A mid-tier bank quietly amplifies every shock. The dangerous bank is not the biggest one: it sits in the periphery of the network and multiplies whatever hits it. Vulnerability that only shows up under stress is exactly what a frozen sampler misses.
verdict: Both samplers converge here, but the quantum arm's chi error stays roughly 1.4x lower and its rho reaches 0.986 vs 0.916 -- the amplifier ranks correctly sooner and more sharply.

title: Rival Alliances
story: Two alliances whose guarantees cancel each other out. Frustrated loops of guarantees mean no arrangement pleases everyone -- the energy landscape is rugged for every method. This is the honest control: both samplers agree, and the gallery says so.
verdict: No time-to-accuracy gap: both rank correctly from the shortest prefix. Reported as a control, not a win -- the mechanism needs a two-basin landscape, and frustration destroys the double well here.
